learning: If s-bend and slalom line_loss_events fall to 0 with max_error below 0.055 m, sensing reach was the constraint, so keep the span. If they stay at 1 with max_error at or above 0.06 m, the geometry is at its range and the next gains must come from the controller. If oval progress falls below 0.12, the track narrowing is the likely cause.
notes: Complete robot for the Builder's sensor-reach test: the Builder's geometry (±0.054 m span, 0.027 m steps, mass 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.09 m) with the unchanged iteration 3 controller. Only the sensor span differs from the last race, so the result reads cleanly.
rationale: The Builder's geometry widens the five-sensor span to ±0.054 m at 0.027 m steps, keeps mass 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.09 m, and sensor_size 0.012 m. I pass that geometry through unchanged. The evidence for the controller is the same across iterations 1 to 3: s-bend and slalom each lost the line once per run, with max_error 0.061 to 0.067 m, and oval progress held at about 0.121. Nothing in the race data shows a gain problem. Steering oscillation stayed in a low range on all tracks (0.075 to 0.162), and the robot leaves the track by drift rather than by oscillating. Because signal = reading-weighted average of the weights, the sensor span changes which sensors see the tape but not the signal scale, so the existing weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1] still map an offset to a signal of the same sign and similar size. I therefore keep every controller value from iteration 3 (kp 4.0, ki 0.2, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.3, last_direction, same weights). Changing gains now would confound the sensor-reach test the Builder asked for and the feedback relies on. The observation request covers every measurement needed to read the result, including max_error, line_loss_events and progress on each track.
